statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-114157 (GHSA-7phj-vgxq-r67h) is an ASP.NET Core security feature bypass in the Kestrel named-pipe transport: a listener configured with CurrentUserOnly can lose protected namespace ownership while it recovers, allowing another local user to claim the pipe path. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 8.0.34 and lists Windows as the affected platform (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-7phj-vgxq-r67h, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/507, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 8.0.34-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v8.0.134 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v8.0.134). Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships the ASP.NET Core shared framework at its own .NET version, in aspnetcore8-runtime and in the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap: 8.0.23 through 8.0.33 in the earlier builds and 8.0.34 in both 8.0.34-r0 builds, and each of those shared frameworks contains Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Transport.NamedPipes.dll. On Linux, UseNamedPipes throws PlatformNotSupportedException (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v8.0.33/src/Servers/Kestrel/Transport.NamedPipes/src/WebHostBuilderNamedPipeExtensions.cs), so this owner cannot open a named-pipe listener through it. The decision is FIXED rather than not affected because the vulnerable code ships in every earlier build and 8.0.34-r0 carries Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 8.0.34-r0, the first published build with the fix.
